To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) we present the first fully automated deep learning based approach to bone age assessment and (2) we show that the suggested approach outperforms the state-of-the-art methods.

(a) deep learning methods outperform common methods for bone-age assessment; (b) the performance of deep learning methods depends on the type of hand image used; (c) the deep learning approach can be used to predict the stage of skeletal development; and (d) deep learning models trained on the whole hand images outperform those trained only on the wrist images.

(1) we propose a novel deep learning approach to bone age assessment; (2) we demonstrate that our approach outperforms the current methods; and (3) we show that the performance of our approach is comparable to the performance of human experts.

the problem of bone-age assessment using deep learning.
